system_description.narrative_title: Midterm Turmoil: Trump, White House Chaos, and Election Survival
system_description.narrative_summary: The single dominant narrative is the 2026 US midterm election as a pressure point where Donald Trump’s campaign and Republican survival efforts collide with White House instability, record-low approval, massive donor spending, and legal/institutional battles. As an open system it consists of interacting actors (candidates, staff, donors, courts, media, voters), flows of money, information and legal actions, and is porous to economic shocks and international events; feedbacks among polls, spending, staffing changes and court rulings amplify uncertainty. Near-term catalysts (polls, staff turnover, high-profile legal rulings, donor moves) drive rapid dynamics, while longer-term structural variables (party coalitions, institutional norms, economic conditions) shape resilience or breakdown.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary: federal and key state-level election campaigns (candidates, staff, party machinery), White House operations, congressional races, donors and super PACs, voters and polling, media and information flows, federal courts and high-profile legal cases, economic signals that affect voter sentiment and campaign messaging.
system_description.super_system: The broader U.S. democratic-political order embedded in the global geopolitical and economic system
adjacent_subsystems: Judiciary and legal institutions (Supreme Court, federal courts, election litigation)
Media and information ecosystem (press, leaks, polls, social platforms)
Political finance and donor networks (super PACs, wealthy benefactors, corporate giving)
State-level electoral administration and local politics

variables.name: Campaign funding flow
variables.description: Rate and volume of monetary contributions and expenditures directed to electoral campaigns and allied outside groups.

variables.name: Outside spending flow
variables.description: Rate and volume of independent political spending from non-campaign actors into electoral contests.

variables.name: Donor concentration
variables.description: Share of total political financial resources controlled by a small set of large donors or funding sources.

variables.name: Media attention
variables.description: Overall volume and prominence of coverage that political actors and issues receive across news and social platforms.

variables.name: Information flow rate
variables.description: Speed, reach and frequency of dissemination of political information and misinformation through formal and informal channels.

variables.name: Candidate approval
variables.description: Aggregate level of favorable public evaluation toward a principal political actor or ticket among the electorate.

variables.name: Polling volatility
variables.description: Short-term variability and noise in opinion polls and poll-based indicators of electoral support.

variables.name: Voter engagement level
variables.description: Degree of voter interest, turnout intention, and active participation in campaign-related activities.

variables.name: Campaign staff capacity
variables.description: Size, organizational capability and logistical resources available to campaign and election operations.

variables.name: Staffing turnover rate
variables.description: Rate at which key personnel are replaced or depart within campaign and executive operations.

variables.name: Legal action pressure
variables.description: Intensity and frequency of legal filings, investigations and litigation that affect political actors and campaigns.

variables.name: Judicial unpredictability
variables.description: Degree of uncertainty around judicial decision-making and the likelihood of surprise or divergent rulings.

variables.name: Executive stability
variables.description: Operational steadiness and continuity of the executive office, including internal coordination and crisis resilience.

variables.name: Message coherence
variables.description: Consistency and clarity of political messaging across actors and channels and the degree to which narratives align with strategy.

variables.name: Race competitiveness
variables.description: Closeness of electoral contests measured by expected margins and the distribution of contestable seats.

variables.name: Economic sentiment index
variables.description: Aggregate voter perception of current and expected economic conditions that influence political preferences.

catalysts.title: 2026 US midterm election day
catalysts.description: Nationwide midterm voting and immediate results that will determine control of Congress and shape post-election litigation and messaging.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'What you need to know about the 2026 US midterm elections'; 'The midterm election outcomes that could shape Trump's final two years.'

catalysts.title: Last-ditch super-PAC and outside spending surge
catalysts.description: Major ad buys and independent expenditures from MAGA Inc, super PACs and wealthy donors intensify in key races through the final pre-election stretch.
catalysts.rationale: 'Trump-aligned super PACs pour millions'; 'MAGA Inc unleashes $277 million'; 'Trump pledges to spend $400mn.'

catalysts.title: Ongoing White House staffing turmoil
catalysts.description: Rapid staff departures and public missteps in the West Wing continue, undermining coordination and campaign messaging in the run-up to midterms.
catalysts.rationale: 'White House chaos overshadows Donald Trump’s midterms push'; 'Katie Zacharia fired after five days.'

catalysts.title: Trump rallies and policy bailout push
catalysts.description: Trump's in-person rallies and promises of cash/bailouts (farm aid, tips program) accelerate to woo worried voters before the election.
catalysts.rationale: 'Trump to rally for Graham'; 'Trump Promises Cash and Bailouts'; 'Trump Hands Out $8 Billion to Farmers.'

catalysts.title: Post-election legal preparations and challenges
catalysts.description: Campaigns and aligned groups prepare and file litigation after election results, including hiring lawyers and pre-positioning challenges.
catalysts.rationale: 'The Race Is On for Trump Staffers to Hire Lawyers in Case Democrats Win Midterms'; 'DOJ seeks to bar Minnesota judges...'

catalysts.title: Surge of Justice Dept election watchers
catalysts.description: States prepare for a notable increase in federal observers and legal monitors deployed to monitor midterm administration and election integrity.
catalysts.rationale: 'Monitoring the monitors: US states prepare for surge of Justice Dept election watchers.'

catalysts.title: Corporate and wealthy donor flood into state AG and Senate races
catalysts.description: High-dollar donations target attorney-general and tight Senate contests, concentrating financial influence in specific races ahead of the vote.
catalysts.rationale: 'Corporate donations flood US attorneys-general election races'; 'The Wealthy Donors Fueling Trump’s Final Election Push.'

catalysts.title: Supreme Court docket of high-profile cases
catalysts.description: Pending high-profile Supreme Court matters (race in admissions, 1868 distilling ban) proceed, shaping legal and political narratives ahead of and after midterms.
catalysts.rationale: 'US Supreme Court to hear Maryland case involving race in school admissions'; 'US Supreme Court to review 1868 federal ban on home distilling.'
